en: Salutations to Śiva, the consort of Ambā, the moon-crested Śaṅkara, who is eternally joyful in his divine mind, who tears asunder the accumulation [of karma] during his wanderings within the interior of the lotus, who is the self of consciousness, who has cast away all water [of worldly existence], who possesses a body that is not a body of water, and who shines with a form beyond the physical.
Salutations, salutations to the one of eight forms; salutations to the one of equal fame; salutations, salutations to the Great Self; salutations to the bestower of auspiciousness.
Homage to the one whose heart is moist with compassion; homage be to the one clad in animal skin...

2 Homage to Bhava, whose nature cannot be known even by Brahmā and the other gods, whose feet are worshipped equally by all the deities, and who possesses the power of the excellent jewels and virtues of Śakra... 3
Contemplating "I am Śiva," may Śiva protect you with his auspiciousness, O Śiva! O you of full splendor, worship your own two feet which possess their own radiance.
There exists nothing higher than Śiva; obeisance to Śiva, who sets the world in motion...

(4) Obeisance to Kapardin, who resembles the fire born from wood (kṛpīṭayoni), the sun, and the moon; to the one who dwells in truth within the lotus-heart of the minds of the foremost among those whose wealth is austerity.

Salutations... adorned with ornaments of serpents whose hoods and hoods flash with light. 5 Salutations... who acts as a bee upon the lotus-face of Śivā; who brings delight; who bestows the splendor of ten million suns upon the directions; and who is solely intent on looking upon his own sister Ambā with affection. 6

Salutations to the one who possesses a fierce intellect like the thundering roar of a waterfall tumbling over the slopes of matted locks; to the one whose crest-pennants whirl in agitation at the sound of that roar; to the wielder of the trident, who is formidable against the circles of his enemies and who sports with the elephants of the quarters subdued by the strength of his arms.
Salutations to the one who roams and plays, having conquered the pride and rutting flow of the elephants of the quarters which were swollen with immense arrogance.

Salutations... to the one who removes the heart's longing among those of beautiful vision, the one who rends [all bonds]... 8 Salutations... to the one who performs a fierce *tāṇḍava* dance that delights the sound of the blazing, unbroken mass of his staff-like arms, which are like elephants;
to the one who bestows the friendship of the virtuous upon the Lord of Wealth (Kubera)... 9

Salutations always to You, whose fame is the remains of the food of distinguished devotees who bow down; whose desired form is the nourishment for the worlds, both joyful and enraged, and both wicked and well-nourished; and whose sprout-like lower lip is bitten by the mountain-born Pārvatī according to Your will.
Or salutations to Hara, or to Hari, the one who delights the people, the one who brings joy, the one who dispels weariness, the eternal one, the lord of beings, and the one who extends to all.
Salutations to the eternal one, the Lord of the lords of ascetics, whose form is the universe...

11 Salutations to you, Bhava, possessed of divine majesty; to him whose heart is gladdened by the fire of the eye; to the increaser who wields the bow that supports the vast earth; to him who is praised by those whose wealth is increased by prosperity and who have crushed their enemies... 12

Salutations... to the one who possesses the fullness of all arts, who delights Śivā, and whose hair is like a mountain of swarms of young blue bees emerging from a face beautiful with a smile as lovely as a lotus filled with honey. Thus ends the *Śrīcandramaulīśvarabhujaṅgastotra*, composed by the venerable teacher Śaṅkarānanda.
